subject: Coupa invite accepted but SSO login fails — IDP claim mismatch (Crestline)
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@crestline.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Crestline IDP Admin <idp-admin@crestline.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite — accepted but can't log in

Hi Sean,

We accepted the Coupa invite your team sent this morning (thank you) but when our users try to 'Log in with SSO' they're looped back to the partner login page with a brief 403 and then an error that says "No linked user found". We tried the invite link from an incognito window and cleared cookies — same result. Attached is a screenshot of the error and a short description of what we see.

We also noticed the user that accepted the invite has an email at crestonline.com while our IDP primary attribute is userPrincipalName (upn). Could that be related? Happy to provide any traces you need.

Alex
Director of Procurement
Crestline Manufacturing
Attachment: screenshot_coupa_error.png
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@crestline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite — accepted but can't log in

Thanks Alex — sorry for the friction. I can confirm the invite created a supplier portal user on our side (we see an account tied to the invited email). My suspicion is the SSO attribute mapping: Redwood's Coupa connector currently matches on the "email" claim by default but many enterprise IDPs are configured to assert "upn" or "userPrincipalName".

Ben and Kim — could you take a look at the SAML logs and confirm which claim is arriving from Crestline's assertion? Alex, if you can have your IDP admin share the SAML trace (or turn on debug on the assertion) that will help. I've attached a short guide to the mapping we expect and a link to the ticket where I'll track updates.

Temporary workaround: if someone can log in via the invited email/password flow we can manually link the SSO identity to that supplier profile — but I'd prefer a mapping fix.

Sean
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Coupa invite — accepted but can't log in

Looping in my SSO notes. I captured the SAML trace Alex forwarded earlier and the assertion does include an identifier, but the assertion only provides 'upn' and 'eduPersonPrincipalName' — there is no 'mail' attribute. Our current mapping expects either 'mail' or an 'email' claim. Without it, the Coupa user isn't linked to the SSO subject and we fall back to the "No linked user" path.

I've attached a sanitized saml-trace.txt with the relevant attribute section highlighted. Recommended fixes:
- Crestline IDP: add an outgoing attribute "mail" (user's RFC2822 address) or map 'upn' -> 'email' for this relying party.
- On Redwood: we can add a temporary mapping to check 'upn' if you want to avoid a change on the IDP side; however that change requires a config push and ~30min maintenance window.

If Crestline is comfortable changing their mapping, that's the fastest. If not, I'll schedule the mapping change on our side and run through QA.

Ben
SRE, Integrations
Attachment: saml-trace.txt
From: Crestline IDP Admin <idp-admin@crestline.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite — accepted but can't log in

Thanks for the quick analysis. We enabled the 'mail' attribute for the Relying Party and have re-tested: users can now hit the Coupa SSO flow and land on a logged-in session. However, a different problem surfaced — several of our users log in but do not see any POs or supplier-specific data. After digging we discovered two accounts were created for the same person: one by the invite (local supplier profile) and one by the SSO path. They are separate internal IDs on your side, so the SSO-authenticated account has no PO visibility.

We can either:
- Have Redwood merge the two supplier accounts for the impacted users, OR
- We can re-invite users after we confirm their SSO-linked account (painful at scale).

Can you advise next steps and the information you need from us to perform a merge safely? We are ready to provide a list of impacted email addresses.

—Crestline IT
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Crestline IDP Admin <idp-admin@crestline.com>, alex.torres@crestline.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coupa invite — accepted but can't log in (merge plan)

Hi Alex / Crestline IT — thanks for the update and for enabling 'mail'. Good news that users can authenticate. For account merging we have a two-step safe flow:

1) Provide a vetted list (CSV) of impacted addresses + the invite timestamp. We'll run an initial join on primary email and 'legacy_supplier_id' to detect duplicates.
2) We'll run a dry-run merge in our staging environment and share results (which records will combine and which fields are overridden).
3) Once approved, we schedule a maintenance window where we perform the merge and re-index PO visibility (typically ~20–40 minutes for a small batch).

Temporary workaround: until the merge is complete, any public PO or invoice link can be emailed directly to the impacted user (we can also add them to a temporary reader role if access is urgent).

Action items: Crestline — please send the CSV to sup-onboard@redwood.ai and include any relevant supplier IDs. Ben / Sean — I'll coordinate the dry-run and share the certificate that indicates which records are safe to merge.

I'll schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through the dry-run unless you prefer a different time: https://cal.redwood.ai/kim/30 (proposed).

Thanks — Kim
Partner Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
